grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, cherries, almonds, seeds, tahini, vanilla and lemon are all whole foods or simple cupboard staples, with no jarred sauces, plant milks or sweeteners.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is stocked at Tesco, and British cherries in late June are at their most affordable.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, knife and fork, and stoning cherries with a knife is within any beginner's reach.

works.reason: 200g oats to 600ml water plus crushed fruit and ground almonds sets to a sensible overnight-oat texture for four, with sweetness from the cherries and vanilla and a splash of water to adjust in the morning.

honest_times.reason: Halving and stoning 400g of cherries, chopping almonds and zesting a lemon fits roughly within 15 minutes, and the overnight soak is honestly shown as unattended time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, including the seeds, the chopped almonds and the lemon, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A cold, no-cook breakfast suits midsummer, and cherries are both stirred through and piled on top, so they are clearly the point.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English instructions with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, fruit, nuts, seeds and tahini make a filling, wholesome breakfast a family would happily repeat.
